title: First recordings: Les Hite and Art Tatum
summary: The first recordings with Hite, then a 1938-ish four-side date with Art Tatum, with Royal on clarinet.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Uh-huh. When was the first time you (inaudible)?
That's hard to remember. One of the first -- I don't know. Gee, that's hard to remember. Can't remember first recording.
Because you recorded with Les Height's band.
No, that's probably the first. After that, the next time I recorded was with Art Tatum.
Here in Los Angeles around 1938 or something. We made four sides. Art -- I think he called them "Art Tatum and his Swingsters," or something like that.

Well, it was one -- I played clarinet on the record. Lloyd Reese (PHONETIC) played trumpet. Oscar Bradley (PHONETIC) played drums. Can't think who played bass. That was about it. And Art Tatum played piano. Can't think -- Red Callender, I think, played bass.
Do you know what you recorded? (Inaudible)?
a tune called "I Got My Love to Keep Me Warm," "Plenty of Money and You," and "Body and Soul," and some other tune. It's four sides. That was around '38, '39 era, maybe '37. I don't know.
Did you work with Art any other time?
Just on the recordings. We used to jam every night after work.
